label: Claude Sonnet 5.5
output:
To: lindqvist-family-blog
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Big news: Fernhollow Photo is official!

Ok, deep breath. I've typed and deleted this opening like six times, so I'm just going to say it.

I'm going out on my own. Fernhollow Photo is a real, legal, actual business, and I am a person who owns one now!!

I wanted you all to hear it here first, from me, with a little time to let it sink in before we're all squished around Ruthie's table on the 26th. So here's the whole story, and then you can ask me anything over pie.

**How we got here**

Marisol told me on October 6th that Rosebud Lane was closing at the end of the month. I've shot for her for four years. Four years! I started as the person carrying her bags and somehow ended up leading weddings on my own. Anything good in my photos, I either learned from her or stole from her, and she's fine with that. She taught me how to read a room, how to keep a nervous couple breathing, and how to be calm when the timeline is falling apart and the cake is melting. Marisol, if you're reading this (and I know you will be), thank you. Truly. I would not be doing any of this without you.

Rosebud Lane closed on schedule. And instead of panicking (ok, I panicked a little), I realized I'd been quietly getting ready for this for a long time.

**The part where I tell you I'm not reckless**

I know how this sounds. "Quit the steady thing, start the scary thing, right before winter." But I want you to know I've been planning this in my head for about two years. It's just that now it's out of my head and onto actual paper. Here's where things stand:

- **14 weddings are already booked for 2027.** Six came from Marisol, who sent over couples she couldn't keep and told them I was the one. The other eight found me on their own, which still makes my brain go a little fuzzy. June is my busiest month with four weddings, and the furthest one out is up at Wallowa Lake in September. (Sam, you're coming to that one. It's gorgeous and there's a lake.)
- **I have a second shooter.** Jae is going to second shoot the big weddings with me, paid per wedding. Having a second set of hands (and a second set of knees, since mine are officially retired) is going to make a big difference.
- **Health insurance is handled.** I picked a marketplace plan on November 5th and it starts January 1st. Dad, this one's for you. I love you, I know where it comes from, and it's done. You can put the speech away. Or save it for the pie, I'll still listen.
- **The website is live,** and the LLC is filed.

I'm not going to pretend it isn't scary, because it is. Working for yourself means you're the photographer, the accountant, the email person, and the one who has to remember to back everything up. But it's the good kind of scary, the kind where you're nervous because you actually care about it. And I have a plan, a real one, and some very good people around me.

**The first booking that was 100% mine**

I have to tell you about Dahlia and Ken. On November 7th I got an email from Dahlia that said "We're in!!" and I screamed so loud that Pickle left the room. They're getting married June 12th at Timberline, and they're my first booking that came entirely from me, with no referral. They found me through the photos I took of a couple at Multnomah Falls, and that's what sold them. A couple I photographed for fun, in the rain, with my hair in my face, turned into my first real client. I'm still a little emotional about it.

**The LLC filing, a love story**

I filed the paperwork for Fernhollow Photo LLC on October 22nd. On my lunch break. In my car. In the parking lot outside a Fred Meyer. I hit submit, sat there for a minute, and cried a little, the happy kind, mixed with some "oh my gosh what did I just do." Then I went in and bought groceries, because that's life.

Sam, being the best, made a celebration cake. It said FERNHOLLOW across the top, except he spelled it FERNHOLOW. We looked at it for a moment, and then we ate it anyway. It was delicious. The business is officially named after a cake typo in spirit, and I love it.

**Where the name comes from**

This part is for Grandma.

Fernhollow is named after the fern hollow trail behind Grandma's old place in Gresham. That's where I took my first real pictures, using Grandma's Pentax. I was a kid with a camera that was way too heavy, shooting ferns and wet logs and probably about forty blurry photos of my own shoes. But that's where I first figured out that I loved noticing things and keeping them.

Grandma, the name is for you. Every time I put it on a contract or a website or a lens cloth, it's going to be you and that trail. I hope that's ok. I hope you like it. I kind of think you will.

**A Thanksgiving ask**

Now that the secret's out, I'd love your help with something. I'm bringing my camera to Ruthie's on the 26th, and I'd love to take free family pictures of anyone who wants them. Couples, kids, cousins, grandparents, whoever. Nothing fancy, no stiff poses, no "everybody say cheese." Just good light and everyone being their regular selves (Uncle Greg, I'll let you pick which side is your good one).

It's a thank-you for all the support, and honestly, it'll help me too. Every family photo I take keeps me practicing and keeps me doing what I love. If you want in, just leave a comment below or grab me when we get there. I'll try to catch everyone before dinner, because after dinner nobody wants to move.

**What I'm asking for**

If you're feeling excited for me, great, I'll take it and I'll hold onto it. If you're feeling a little worried, I get that too, and it's ok to say so. I'd just ask you to trust that I've done my homework. If you know anyone getting married in 2027 or beyond, or anyone who needs good photos of anything, send them my way. That's the biggest help you can give me.

And if you just want to tell me congratulations, I'd really love that too. I've been holding this in for weeks and it feels so good to finally say it out loud.

I'll see you all at Ruthie's. I'm bringing the rolls and the cranberry thing, and Sam is driving.

Love you all so much. Thanks for being my first and favorite audience.

Tessa

P.S. Pickle has no opinion on any of this, but he did eat part of a camera strap this week, so he's definitely involved in the business now.
